[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the core components using **BODMAS**: 58 × 2 = 116 and (43 + 15) = 58.

Simplify: 116 − 58 = 58.

Remaining: 58 − 29 + 64 + 18.

Total: 29 + 82 = 111.

**∴ The correct answer is 111.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** 58 × 2 − 29 + 64 − (43 + 15) + 18

Apply the **BODMAS rule** (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction):

⇒ 116 − 29 + 64 − (58) + 18

⇒ 116 − 29 + 64 − 58 + 18

⇒ (116 + 64 + 18) − (29 + 58)

⇒ 198 − 87

⇒ 111

**∴ The correct answer is 111.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

The acronym stands for **Bracket**, **Of** (Orders/Exponents), **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**, which defines the sequence of operations.

Bracket Hierarchy

Always solve **Parentheses ()** first, followed by **Braces {}**, and then **Square Brackets []**.

Commutative Property

For **Addition** and **Multiplication**, the order of numbers does not change the result (e.g., a + b = b + a).

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve using the **unit digit** method to save time.

Expression unit digits: 3 + 6 − 4 + (3 × 2) + 7

⇒ 3 + 6 − 4 + 6 + 7 = 18

The **unit digit** of the result must be 8.

Among the given options, only 128 ends with the digit 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 128.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 33 + 76 − 44 + (23 × 2) + 17

Follow the **BODMAS** rule: **B**rackets, **O**rders, **D**ivision, **M**ultiplication, **A**ddition, **S**ubtraction.

⇒ 33 + 76 − 44 + 46 + 17

⇒ (33 + 76 + 46 + 17) − 44

⇒ 172 − 44

⇒ 128

**∴ The correct answer is 128.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

This rule dictates the **hierarchy of mathematical operations** to ensure consistent results. Multiplication must be performed before addition or subtraction when no brackets or orders are involved.

Commutative Property of Addition

Addition is **commutative**, meaning a + b = b + a. In simplification, it is often easier to sum all positive terms first and then subtract the negative terms.

questions.question: ((0.5)⁴-(0.4)⁴)/((0.5)²-(0.4)²)=?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the expression as a form of (a⁴ − b⁴) ÷ (a² − b²).

By **algebraic identity**, (a⁴ − b⁴) = (a² − b²)(a² + b²).

The expression simplifies directly to a² + b².

Put a = 0.5 and b = 0.4: (0.5)² + (0.4)² = 0.25 + 0.16 = 0.41.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.41.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Expression = ((0.5)⁴ − (0.4)⁴) ÷ ((0.5)² − (0.4)²)

**Formula Used:** x² − y² = (x − y)(x + y)

⇒ Let a = 0.5 and b = 0.4

⇒ Expression = ((a²)² − (b²)²) ÷ (a² − b²)

⇒ Expression = [(a² − b²)(a² + b²)] ÷ (a² − b²)

⇒ Expression = a² + b²

⇒ Expression = (0.5)² + (0.4)²

⇒ Expression = 0.25 + 0.16

⇒ Expression = 0.41

**∴ The correct answer is 0.41.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference of Squares

The identity a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) is one of the most common **algebraic factorizations** used in simplification.

Higher Power Identities

The pattern for even powers follows aⁿ − bⁿ = (aⁿ/² − bⁿ/²)(aⁿ/² + bⁿ/²), allowing for **recursive simplification**.

Decimal Squaring

When squaring a decimal with one decimal place, the result will have **two decimal places** (e.g., 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25).

questions.question: The product of the three consecutive odd numbers is 12075. What is the largest of the three numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Approximate the **cube root** of the product to find the middle value: √³12075 ≈ 22.9.

The **consecutive odd numbers** near 22.9 are 21, 23, and 25.

Verify the product: 21 × 23 × 25 = 483 × 25 = 12075.

The **largest** number among 21, 23, and 25 is 25.

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Product of three **consecutive odd numbers** = 12075.

**Method:** Prime Factorization of the product.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/77cbe399453e7ce8d772a2a339f97d87a54017e69d741f0295e8c02062814c0a.png] 

⇒ Prime factors of 12075:

⇒ 12075 = 5 × 2415

⇒ 12075 = 5 × 5 × 483

⇒ 12075 = 5 × 5 × 3 × 161

⇒ 12075 = 5 × 5 × 3 × 7 × 23

Group these factors into three **consecutive odd numbers**:

⇒ (3 × 7) × 23 × (5 × 5)

⇒ 21 × 23 × 25

The numbers are 21, 23, and 25.

⇒ Largest number = 25.

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Consecutive Odd Numbers

These are odd integers that follow each other in order, such as x, x+2, x+4. The common difference is always 2.

Arithmetic Mean of Consecutive Numbers

For an odd number of terms in an arithmetic progression, the **middle term** is the average of the numbers.

Product Approximation

If the product of three consecutive numbers is P, the middle number is approximately √³P.

questions.question: If a = 0.067, then what is the value of sqrt{4a² + 4a + 1} + 3a ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **perfect square identity**: 4a² + 4a + 1 = **(2a + 1)²**.

The expression reduces to √(2a + 1)² + 3a = **2a + 1 + 3a = 5a + 1**.

Substituting **a = 0.067**, we get **5(0.067) + 1 = 0.335 + 1 = 1.335**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.335.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Value of **a = 0.067**

**Formula Used:**

Algebraic identity: **(x + y)² = x² + 2xy + y²**

Property: **√x² = |x|**

**Calculations:**

⇒ √(4a² + 4a + 1) + 3a

⇒ √((2a)² + 2 × (2a) × 1 + 1²) + 3a

⇒ √(2a + 1)² + 3a

⇒ (2a + 1) + 3a

⇒ 5a + 1

⇒ 5 × 0.067 + 1

⇒ 0.335 + 1

⇒ 1.335

**∴ The correct answer is 1.335.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perfect Square Binomial

An expression of the form x² + 2xy + y² can always be written as (x + y)², which simplifies the square root to (x + y) for positive terms.

Absolute Value in Roots

Mathematically, √x² = |x|. If the variable x is known to be such that the binomial is positive (like 2a + 1 where a = 0.067), the modulus is simply the term itself.

Decimal Calculations

When multiplying decimals like 5 × 0.067, multiply as whole numbers (5 × 67 = 335) and then place the decimal point three places from the right to get 0.335.

questions.question: The area of a rhombus is 336 cm². One of the diagonal is 14 cm. What is the side (in cm) of the rhombus?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the second **diagonal**: d₂ = (2 × **Area**) ÷ d₁ = (2 × 336) ÷ 14 = 48 cm.

The **half-diagonals** are 7 cm (14 ÷ 2) and 24 cm (48 ÷ 2).

Using the **Pythagorean triplet** (7, 24, 25), the **side** of the **rhombus** is 25 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Area** of **rhombus** = 336 cm²

Diagonal 1 (d₁) = 14 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area = 1/2 × d₁ × d₂

**Side** (a) = √[(d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)²]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/574fb50959590e49cbca91d0fc5975b7a31a8c5cf79e18be373b117d281727c7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 336 = 1/2 × 14 × d₂

⇒ 336 = 7 × d₂

⇒ d₂ = 336 ÷ 7 = 48 cm

⇒ **Side** = √[(14/2)² + (48/2)²]

⇒ **Side** = √(7² + 24²)

⇒ **Side** = √(49 + 576)

⇒ **Side** = √625

⇒ **Side** = 25 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 25 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Rhombus

A **rhombus** is a special **parallelogram** where all four sides are **equal**. Its **diagonals** bisect each other at **right angles** (90°).

Relationship between Side and Diagonals

The side 'a' and diagonals d₁, d₂ are related by the equation: 4a² = d₁² + d₂².

Perimeter of Rhombus

Since all sides are **equal**, the **perimeter** of a rhombus is calculated as 4 × side.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Number of terms (**n**) = [(Last term − First term) ÷ Common difference] + 1

⇒ **n** = [(272 − 96) ÷ 4] + 1 = 44 + 1 = 45

Sum = Average × **n** = [(96 + 272) ÷ 2] × 45

Sum = 184 × 45 = 8280

**∴ The correct answer is 8280.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First term (**a**) = 96

Common difference (**d**) = 100 − 96 = 4

Last term (**l**) = 272

**Formula Used:**

n-th term: **l** = **a** + (**n** − 1)**d**

Sum of **n** terms: **Sₙ** = (**n**/2) × (**a** + **l**)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/734f751b6d39a0dd9e69d4bfb074c50cc3ccab76f7604c5bafc74eb7658aac6f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 272 = 96 + (**n** − 1) × 4

⇒ 272 − 96 = (**n** − 1) × 4

⇒ 176 = (**n** − 1) × 4

⇒ **n** − 1 = 176 ÷ 4 = 44

⇒ **n** = 44 + 1 = 45

⇒ **S₄₅** = (45/2) × (96 + 272)

⇒ **S₄₅** = (45/2) × 368

⇒ **S₄₅** = 45 × 184 = 8280

**∴ The correct answer is 8280.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

General Term of an AP

The **n**-th term is given by **aₙ** = **a** + (**n** − 1)**d**, where **a** is the first term and **d** is the common difference.

Sum of First n Natural Numbers

The sum of the first **n** natural numbers is **S** = **n**(**n** + 1) ÷ 2.

Arithmetic Mean

For any two numbers **x** and **y**, the arithmetic mean is (**x** + **y**) ÷ 2.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ The series is an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)** with first term 116 and common difference 4. Total terms (n) = [(Last − First) ÷ Difference] + 1 n = [(352 − 116) ÷ 4] + 1 = 59 + 1 = 60 terms. Sum = (n ÷ 2) × (First + Last) = (60 ÷ 2) × (116 + 352) = 30 × 468. **∴ The correct answer is 14040.**

questions.question: The average of 24 numbers is 48. A number 'M' is subtracted from each number. New average of these 24 numbers is 39. What is the value of 'M'?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ If a constant value **'M'** is subtracted from every observation in a set, the **Average** of that set also decreases by exactly **'M'**. **Change in Average** = **Old Average** − **New Average** **M** = 48 − 39 = 9 **∴ The correct answer is 9.**

questions.question: What is the Highest Common Factor of 0.42, 0.60 and 0.78?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the decimals into **integers** by multiplying by 100: 42, 60, and 78.

Calculate the **differences** between the numbers: 60 − 42 = 18 and 78 − 60 = 18.

The **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** must be a factor of 18. Factors of 18 are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18.

The largest factor that divides 42, 60, and 78 is **6**.

Re-apply the decimal by dividing by 100: 6 ÷ 100 = 0.06.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.06.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Decimal numbers 0.42, 0.60, and 0.78.

**Formula Used:** HCF of decimals = (HCF of integers obtained by making decimal places equal) ÷ (10ⁿ), where n is the number of decimal places.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d779872eb0f8b98a8fbb4aa1f01adbea66ea41a888423d32364cc026fde8b6f7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Express decimals as fractions: 42/100, 60/100, 78/100

⇒ To find the **HCF**, we find the **prime factorization** of the numerators:

⇒ 42 = 2 × 3 × 7

⇒ 60 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 2² × 3 × 5

⇒ 78 = 2 × 3 × 13

⇒ Common factors are 2 and 3. So, HCF(42, 60, 78) = 2 × 3 = 6.

⇒ Applying the common denominator: 6 ÷ 100 = 0.06.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.06.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF of Fractions

HCF = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators). Ensure fractions are in their simplest form before applying the rule.

LCM of Decimals

Like HCF, first make the number of decimal places equal for all numbers, find the LCM as integers, and then place the decimal point accordingly.

Relationship between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: A × B = HCF × LCM.

questions.question: What is the largest 2 digit number which is exactly divisible by both 2 and 7?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **LCM** of 2 and 7 is **14**.

The **largest 2-digit number** is 99.

99 ÷ 14 = 7 with **remainder 1**.

Largest multiple = 99 − 1 = 98.

**∴ The correct answer is 98.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Divisors are 2 and 7.

**Formula Used:** Common divisibility requires the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7b8e5bf2427ab288afcdff95e98930ba88f07c20bde8944929a0a8dafc6290c4.png] 

⇒ **LCM** of 2 and 7 = 2 × 7 = **14**.

⇒ Multiples of 14 are: 14, 28, 42, 56, 70, 84, 98, 112, ...

⇒ Since we need the **largest 2-digit number**, we check values less than 100.

⇒ 98 is the highest value in the sequence that is less than 100.

**∴ The correct answer is 98.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM (Least Common Multiple)

The **LCM** of two **prime numbers** (like 2 and 7) is simply their product.

Divisibility Rule for 14

A number is divisible by 14 if it is both **even** (divisible by 2) and satisfies the **divisibility rule for 7**.

General Formula for Largest Multiple

To find the largest multiple of **n** less than or equal to **k**, use the formula: **k − (k mod n)**.

questions.question: 18 percent of a number exceeds 12 percent of the same number by 48. What is the value of the number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in percentage values = 18% − 12% = 6%

Given that this 6% difference corresponds to the value **48**.

Calculating 1% of the number: 48 ÷ 6 = 8.

The whole number (100%) = 8 × 100 = 800.

**∴ The correct answer is 800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage 1 = **18%**

Percentage 2 = **12%**

Numerical Difference = **48**

**Formula Used:**

Value = (Difference in Values ÷ Difference in Percentages) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8640095edebf9d0f4f0eb7e7d0cd78a9be097b2036e860a75a95ca1661a93281.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the required **number** be x.

⇒ 18% of x − 12% of x = 48

⇒ (18 − 12)% of x = 48

⇒ 6% of x = 48

⇒ (6 ÷ 100) × x = 48

⇒ x = (48 × 100) ÷ 6

⇒ x = 8 × 100

⇒ x = 800

**∴ The correct answer is 800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Difference Rule

When two different percentages of the same base number are compared, the difference in their values is directly proportional to the difference in their percentage rates.

Base Value Calculation

If p% of a number is 'n', the original number is calculated as: Number = (n × 100) ÷ p.

Successive Percentage Change

If a number changes by a% and then by b%, the net effective change is [a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100]%.

questions.question: The difference between cost price and selling price of an article is Rs. 400. Loss percentage is 20 percent. What is the selling price of the article?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ **Loss Percentage** of 20% is equivalent to the ratio 1/5. This implies if the **Cost Price (CP)** is 5 units, the **Loss** is 1 unit. The **difference** between CP and SP (which is the loss) is given as **₹400**. ⇒ 1 unit = ₹400. **Selling Price (SP)** = CP − Loss = 5 − 1 = 4 units. ⇒ SP = 4 × ₹400 = **₹1600**. **∴ The correct answer is ₹1600.**

Ratio of **Efficiencies** (Wage Ratio) = Inverse of Time Ratio = 5 : 4.

Total wage units = 5 + 4 = 9 units → ₹6300.

1 unit = ₹700.

Share of M = 5 units × 700 = ₹3500.

questions.question: A alone can do a work in 12 days. B alone can do the same work in 18 days. C alone can do the same work in 36 days. They started the work together. B left after 2 days. A and C together completed the remaining work. In how many days remaining work was completed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiencies: A = **3**, B = **2**, C = **1**.

Work done in **2 days** by (A+B+C) = (3 + 2 + 1) × 2 = **12 units**.

**Remaining Work** = 36 − 12 = **24 units**.

Time taken by **A and C** = 24 ÷ (3 + 1) = **6 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 days.**

questions.question: A train moves at a speed of 25 m/s and crosses a bridge of length 700 metres in 45 seconds. What is the length (in metres) of the train?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Total distance covered = **Speed** × **Time** Total distance = 25 × 45 = 1125 m **Train Length** = Total distance − **Bridge Length** Train Length = 1125 − 700 = 425 m **∴ The correct answer is 425 m.**

questions.question: The speed of stream is 4 km/hr. A boat goes 120 km upstream and comes back to the starting point in 40 hours. What is the speed (in km/hr) of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **round trip** (Upstream + Downstream), use the direct formula: **Total Time = [2 × D × u] ÷ [u² − v²]**

Where **D = 120 km**, **v = 4 km/hr**, and **Total Time = 40 hr**.

40 = [2 × 120 × u] ÷ [u² − 4²] ⇒ 40 = 240u ÷ (u² − 16)

1 = 6u ÷ (u² − 16) ⇒ u² − 6u − 16 = 0

Solving the quadratic equation, we get **u = 8** (Since speed cannot be negative).

**∴ The correct answer is 8 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/60ba6c34eb5cc160527368107092c8e1885252f468ebb6f804810d408f8d1b1a.png] 

**Given:**

**Speed of Stream (v)** = 4 km/hr

**Distance (D)** = 120 km

**Total Time (T)** = 40 hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Upstream Speed = u − v | Downstream Speed = u + v

**Calculations:**

⇒ [120 ÷ (u − 4)] + [120 ÷ (u + 4)] = 40

⇒ 120 × [(u + 4) + (u − 4)] ÷ [(u − 4)(u + 4)] = 40

⇒ 120 × [2u] ÷ (u² − 16) = 40

⇒ 240u ÷ (u² − 16) = 40

⇒ 6u = u² − 16

⇒ u² − 6u − 16 = 0

⇒ u² − 8u + 2u − 16 = 0

⇒ u(u − 8) + 2(u − 8) = 0

⇒ (u − 8)(u + 2) = 0

⇒ u = 8 or u = −2

⇒ **Speed of boat in still water (u)** = 8 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 8 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed in Still Water and Stream

Speed of Boat in Still Water (u) = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Speed of Current

Speed of Stream (v) = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Average Speed for Round Trip

Average Speed = (Downstream Speed × Upstream Speed) ÷ Still Water Speed = (u² − v²) ÷ u.

questions.question: When an article is sold for a discount of 20 percent, then there is a profit 25 percent. If the marked price of article is Rs. 1000, then what is the cost price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Cost Price (CP)** to **Marked Price (MP)** is given by: **CP/MP = (100 − Discount%)/(100 + Profit%)**

CP / 1000 = (100 − 20) / (100 + 25)

CP / 1000 = 80 / 125

CP = (80 ÷ 125) × 1000 ⇒ CP = 80 × 8

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 640.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Marked Price (MP)** = Rs. 1000, **Discount** = 20%, **Profit** = 25%.

**Formula Used:** **SP** = **MP** × (100 − D%)/100; **CP** = **SP** × 100/(100 + P%)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dcebb8ea52c988a4d5e1b1288386ebb6898b488c6de7b4aa4dcc586bc2b8caf4.png] 

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 1000 − (20% of 1000)

⇒ **SP** = 1000 − 200 = Rs. 800

⇒ Since **Profit** is 25%, **SP** = 125% of **Cost Price (CP)**

⇒ 800 = 1.25 × **CP**

⇒ **CP** = 800 ÷ 1.25 = Rs. 640

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 640.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CP and MP Relationship

The formula **CP/MP = (100 − Discount%)/(100 + Profit%)** is the fastest way to find the ratio between cost and marked price when both profit and discount percentages are known.

Mark-up Percentage

Mark-up % = [(MP − CP)/CP] × 100. It represents how much the price is increased over the **Cost Price** before offering a discount.

Successive Discounts

If two discounts d₁ and d₂ are given, the equivalent single discount is **d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100**.

questions.question: Marked price of an article is 40 percent more than its cost price. It is sold at a profit of 25 percent. Marked price of article is Rs. 2800. What is the selling price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Marked Price (MP)** to **Cost Price (CP)** = 140 : 100 = 7 : 5.

Given 7 units = ₹2800 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹400.

**Cost Price (CP)** = 5 units = 5 × 400 = ₹2000.

**Profit** = 25% ⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 125% of CP.

**Selling Price (SP)** = 2000 × 1.25 = ₹2500.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Marked Price (MP)** = ₹2800

**Markup Percentage** = 40%

**Profit Percentage** = 25%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6028aa1da38e46640d8fff3f672ddc14bc921fa658f4fc0e956cf7a6796988e6.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Marked Price (MP)** = **Cost Price (CP)** × (1 + Markup%/100)

**Selling Price (SP)** = **Cost Price (CP)** × (1 + Profit%/100)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2800 = CP × (1 + 40/100)

⇒ 2800 = CP × 140/100

⇒ CP = (2800 × 100) ÷ 140

⇒ CP = 20 × 100 = ₹2000

⇒ SP = 2000 × (1 + 25/100)

⇒ SP = 2000 × 125/100

⇒ SP = 20 × 125

⇒ SP = ₹2500

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between CP, MP, and Discount

The core relationship is given by the ratio CP/MP = (100 − Discount%)/(100 + Profit%).

Markup Percentage

Markup % is the percentage by which the **Marked Price** is higher than the **Cost Price**: Markup % = [(MP − CP)/CP] × 100.

Discount and Selling Price

Selling Price is also calculated as SP = MP × (1 − Discount%). In this problem, no discount was mentioned, so SP was derived directly from Profit.
